items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I also played with Art Tatum for the first time during that period. He was working at a place called the St. Francis down on Eighth Street, and he came to town and he wanted some horns to play with him -- because he always did a single or a trio, you know, a duo... So he hired John Anderson and me a

ctx.x: Murray Rappaport owned a record store up on Hollywood Boulevard, just about a block east of Vine. And he would record people. He had recorded Art Tatum, Illinois Jacquet, several people. But this guy was a very shady character, ha-ha!, business-wise. He was about the best (?) I knew. He was the type of guy, if he could make more money doing a legitimate deal, he'd have to lose! Ha-ha...!
